Heard Sri Anil Kumar Srivastava, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sri Ram Bahadur, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Hitesh Pachori, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and Sri Prem Prakash Tiwari, learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

The instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking quashing of the entire criminal proceedings of Complaint Case No. 1809 of 2018 (Yashbhan Singh vs. Manisha and others)
under Sections 323, 406 I.P.C., Police Station-Fatehpur Sikri, District-Agra as well as summoning order dated 06.08.2019.

3. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the applicants submits that the instant complaint is nothing but a counterblast to the complaint filed by the daughter of the applicant no. 1 against the opposite party no. 2 and his family members due to matrimonial discord between the daughter of the applicant no. 1 and son of the opposite party no. 2.
4.

Learned Senior Counsel for the applicants submits that the allegation in the complaint is that when the opposite party no. 2 and his son were not in the house, his daughter-in-law called her mother (applicant no. 1) and her brother (applicant no. 2) in the house of the opposite party no. 2 and took away all the streedhan, jewellery, clothes, etc and went to her paternal house.
Subsequently, when query was made, the opposite party no. 2 realized that the daughter of the applicant no.1 along with her streedhan also took some jewellery of the wife of the opposite party no.2.
With aforesaid allegations, the instant complaint case was filed by the opposite party no.2.

Learned Senior Counsel further submits that the instant complaint is nothing but a counterblast case on the basis of a concocted story to create a defence in the complaint filed by the daughter of the applicant no. 1.
Therefore, he submits that the instant complaint case is nothing but a malicious prosecution on the part of the opposite party no.2 and the same deserves to be quashed.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 though admits the matrimonial discord between the daughter of the applicant no. 1 and the son of the opposite party no. 2; however supports the allegations made in the complaint filed by the opposite party no. 2.

He further submits that the trial court having found a prima facie case against the applicants, has rightly summoned the applicants for trial, therefore, no interference is called for in the instant case while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
6.

Learned A.G.A. also supports the submissions made by learned counsel for the opposite party no.2.
7.
Having heard the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court has carefully gone through the records of the case.
8. From the record of the case, it is apparent that there was matrimonial discord between the daughter of the applicant no. 1 as well as the son of the opposite party no.2.

The daughter of the applicant no. 1 had filed a complaint case under Section 498A I.P.C. and other allied provisions of the I.P.C. as well as the D.P. Act and the instant complaint case was filed by the opposite party no. 2 as a counterblast to the complaint filed by his daughter-in-law.
Therefore, it is apparent that it is a counterblast complaint, hence, the same is nothing but a malicious prosecution on the part of opposite party no.2.
Therefore, in the considered opinion of this Court, the same deserves to be quashed.

9. For the reasons aforesaid, the instant application is allowed and the entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 1809 of 2018 (Yashbhan Singh vs. Manisha and others) under Sections 323,
406 I.P.C., Police Station-Fatehpur Sikri, District-Agra are hereby quashed.
